deviations.what: Plan task t3's acceptance criterion said substance uses 'message LENGTH and reply counts', and the signal set confirmed in c22/q4 included 'thread starts / questions asked'. Neither reply counts nor thread starts is computable from the input: _serialize_message emits only {id, author, content, created_at} — no reply-to reference and no thread-parent field. The t3 agent implemented the closest data-backed proxy, content ending in '?', and named the field 'question_starts' rather than 'thread_starts' to avoid overclaiming; it did not fabricate a reply-count field. The delivered signal set is therefore message_count, distinct_channels, question_starts, substance{total_length,avg_length} — three of the four intended signals plus an honestly-named proxy.
deviations.reason: The adapter does not serialize reply/thread references. Adding them would reopen t2's file (jlab/cli/_discord.py) and widen this ship; the honest alternative was naming the proxy accurately.

deviations.what: t4 passed the c14/h23 isolation guard by splitting a string literal — getattr(member, 'global' + '_name', None) — rather than reading Member.global_name plainly. The guard (tests/test_discord.py::test_upstream_workaround_is_isolated_to_the_adapter) forbids the substring 'global_name' anywhere in jlab/ outside the adapter. That guard is over-broad: it protects the MESSAGE-serialization workaround that discord-bot-cli#14 will replace, but resolve.py reads global_name off a guild.fetch_member result, which is a different seam that #14 does not touch. Fixed at merge by un-obfuscating resolve.py and narrowing the guard with a documented exemption for jlab/members/resolve.py, instead of leaving code hidden from its own guard.
deviations.reason: Obfuscating to satisfy a guard defeats the guard and makes the code worse; the honest fix was to correct the guard's scope to match its stated intent.
